DEPOSITED BY THE
UNITED STATES OF AM

 
B |
AG

Executibe @rder

EXEMPTION OF CurTIS F. MARBUT FROM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
For AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404;
5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch
or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the Dis-
trict of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such
service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided,
That the President may, by Executive order, exempt from the provisions of this
section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *.”

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that Curtis F. Marbut, Chief of
the Division of Soil Survey of the Bureau of Chemistry and Soils, Department of
Agriculture, who was 70 years of age on July 19, 1933, and who was exempted until
June 30, 1934, from compulsory retirement by Executive Order No. 6214, dated
July 25, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued
in the service until July 1, 1935;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid
section, I do hereby exempt Curtis F. Marbut from the provisions thereof and con-
tinue him in the service until July 1, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT.
Tue Wairr Hovss,
June 14, 1984.

[No. 6738]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The single operative paragraph jointly exempts the employee and continues him in service until 1935-07-01. The matching recital confirms this one temporally limited exemption/continuation grant. This is an express temporal limit, not a performance deadline or evidence of actual service, retirement or death. Inclusive reading expires at the end of the stated day; the exclusive alternative expires at its start. No independent perpetual exemption or recurring command remains. No held evidence establishes an earlier cessation; bounded machine searches do not prove universal absence.

source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Curtis F. Marbut, principal soil scientist, Division of Soil Survey, Bureau of Chemistry and Soils, Department of Agriculture, who was 70 years of age on July 19, 1933, and who was exempted until July 1, 1935, from compulsory retirement by Executive Orders Nos. 6214 and 6738, dated July 25, 1933, and June 14, 1934, respectively, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until July 1, 1936;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Curtis F. Marbut from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until July 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

June 19, 1935.

research_rationale: Read complete assigned public GPO page images and all dossier text witnesses. Preserve machine_read_government_printed_copy, acceptable_as_original=false and the original replacement/recheck note. original_confirmed=false: printed signature examined, signed-original authentication not claimed. Read pinned prior research: no prior versions located. Valla provides no automatic approval. USC search omits laws after October 9 through October 14, 2026; OFR starts 1937; Namier misses 85 census texts and 302 unparsed personal names. These are bounded searches, not silence-based endings. Scan 129 has complete Marbut order, Franklin D. Roosevelt printed signature, June 14, 1934 and No. 6738; OCR falsely reads 1984. Scans 127-128 are outside-target/deposit leaf. July 19, 1933 is an age recital; June 30, 1934 belongs to the earlier EO 6214 grant. EO 7080 dated June 19, 1935 acknowledges the existing grants and makes a further exemption until July 1, 1936. Its new operative personal grant does not strike, insert, revoke or replace EO 6738. The later grant sustains permission under its own authority but does not remove EO 6738 own express temporal scope. No conclusion on EO 7080 whole lifecycle is assigned here.

savings_residuals.reason: Full printing contains no express savings or independent operative command. Historical service and accrued compensation or retirement consequences are not extinguished by this conclusion; they do not renew this personal time-limited grant. Bounded citation and personal-name searches located no surviving independent command; OFR pre-1937 and missing held-text limitations remain.
